defectsFixed.after: All five sources are scanned with the same existing glob shape ('contributions/*.json', '*/contributions/*.json'), which was verified empirically to already handle every directory depth present (0-deep for warzone/spring, 1-deep for blizzard/ea, and — via git's default wildcard-crosses-slash pathspec matching, confirmed empirically — 2-deep for other/extensions/<vertical>/contributions). No pattern change was needed, only the two missing array entries.

defectsFixed.before: Only ':(glob)extensions/**/contributions/*.json'. Contributions that relocated out of extensions/** during the 2026-08-30 externalization were invisible.
defectsFixed.after: Added ':(glob)packages/**/contributions/*.json' and ':(glob)examples/**/contributions/*.json'. Verified safe by reading the contract.id of every contribution file under both new roots (packages/**: 41 files; examples/**: 8 files) — the existing 'json.contract?.id !== modkit/codec-contribution' filter already isolates every test fixture (all of them declare org.modkitx/* or x3.demo/* contract ids, never the real modkit/* namespace) and every non-codec contribution kind (viewer/editor/service-provider/contract-definition), so widening the glob could not pull in noise. Also verified no id collisions arise anywhere in the combined internal file set, and that apps/web/dist-app (a checked-in, non-gitignored build-output copy of extensions/**) is not matched by any of the three new patterns, so stale build output cannot shadow source.

defectsFixed.location: check-registry.mjs, the supportState cross-check inside the format-row loop (line ~580 before this change)
defectsFixed.before: const entry = declared === null ? undefined : x3.get(declared); if (entry !== undefined) { /* supportState cross-check */ } — a lookup miss (declared names a contribution the scan does not find) fell through both branches: no fail(), no flagUnavailable(), nothing. The cross-check silently did not run and left no trace that it hadn't.
defectsFixed.after: The miss branch is now explicit: if (declared !== null && entry === undefined) fail(...). Every declared x3ContributionId that cannot be resolved is now itself a reported problem, unconditionally, regardless of allocation.state or of whatever the state-specific rules above already said about the row. Chosen deliberately as a new, always-fires problem() rather than folding it into an existing message, so it cannot be mistaken for having already been covered by a different rule for a different reason.
defectsFixed.verification: Confirmed empirically that every row landing in the new fail branch was previously invisible to it: none of them appear in the new failure message set with any other wording that would have implied the miss, and — separately — that the branch is not merely decorative: format/spring-rapid, format/spring-s3o, format/spring-vfs and format/txt/open-inspect now visibly take the *resolved* branch (their contributions were found once the scan was completed) and their supportState was cross-checked and found consistent.
